audits.title: Using a proforma to improve standards of documentation of an orthopaedic post-take ward round.
audits.standard: GMC and Royal College of Physicians documentation recommendations: clearly documented PTWR, date/time, consultant on take, clinician leading and documenting, presenting complaint and management plan
audits.setting: District general hospital trauma and orthopaedic department (population 320,000, consultant-led 24/7 trauma service)

cycle1.result: 72% seen on PTWR, 47% of these clearly labelled; 64% of those not seen were weekend admissions; no consultant on take identifiable in 19%, presenting complaint missing in 78%, no plan in 3%, not timed in 17%, no name 19%, no signature 14%, no grade 50%, no contact details 25%.

audits.intervention: Trauma Meeting/Post-Take Ward Round proforma on yellow paper, designed with the team (PDSA cycles), results presented at departmental teaching, and weekend surgical juniors briefed to attend the trauma meeting and complete it.

cycle2.period: Prospective re-audit two weeks after implementation
cycle2.result: Not seen on PTWR fell from 28% to 18% (4% weekend admissions); 88% of those seen had a proforma; 18% of all cases had no proforma; consultant unidentifiable in 4%; all entries signed and dated; no name 12%, no contact details 15%, no grade 10%.

audits.title: Making the weekend work: a local quality improvement project to establish and improve the quality of weekend handover.
audits.standard: 10 handover components derived from RCS, RCP and BMA handover guidelines, each with a set standard (some patient identifiers at 100%); aim to raise compliance to 90–100%
audits.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics department, Frimley Park Hospital (750-bed NHS hospital), Surrey

cycle1.result: Baseline (247 handovers over nine weeks): patient name 99%, hospital number 94%, admission reason 91%, other categories 12% to 84% (date of birth 54%, location 84%, frequency of review 70%, TTO 12%); only admission reason met its standard.

audits.intervention: Two-step change: extra columns (TTO, day to be seen, DNAR) added to the Word handover table, then a new intranet handover tool with drop-down boxes, date selector and multiuser access; instruction document given at induction.

cycle2.result: Sustainability re-audit of intranet tool (201 handovers, new cohort of doctors): patient name 100%, hospital number 98%, date of birth 85%; five of 10 categories met their standard (patient name, location, consultant, admission reason, frequency of review); all except TTO were above 50%.

audits.other_findings: After the amended table (257 handovers) TTO rose from 12% to 31% and location fell from 84% to 77%; after the intranet tool (207 handovers) location 90%, consultant 94%, admission reason 97%, frequency of review 100% and TTO 5%. TTO stayed poorest (18%) and was dropped from the tool.
audits.citation: Heller RA, Hu L. Making the weekend work: a local quality improvement project to establish and improve the quality of weekend handover. BMJ Open Qual. 2018;7(3):e000215. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2017-000215. PMID: 30094343.

audits.title: Quality of Trauma Meeting Presentations Before and After Introduction of a Structured Template at a Major Trauma Centre: A Before-and-After Quality Improvement Study.
audits.standard: Locally developed 10-domain, 20-point presentation quality score; complete presentation defined a priori as score ≥ 16
audits.setting: Morning trauma meeting, Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, major trauma centre (Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: Mean score 11.6 ± 3.0/20; complete presentations 18/75 (24.0%); management plan documented 49/75 (65.3%); tasks allocated 28/75 (37.3%); median clarification prompts 2 (IQR 1-3).

audits.intervention: One-page 10-domain structured presentation template expanded from an acronym in the electronic patient record, introduced with a five-minute briefing, laminated copies in the meeting room and inclusion in the junior doctor induction pack.

cycle2.result: Mean score 17.1 ± 2.1/20 (difference 5.5, 95% CI 4.7-6.3; p<0.001); complete presentations 61/75 (81.3%; p<0.001); management plan 72/75 (96.0%); tasks allocated 67/75 (89.3%); median clarification prompts 1 (IQR 0-1).

audits.other_findings: Median presentation duration unchanged (2.7 to 2.5 minutes, p=0.18); neurovascular status improved from 34/75 (45.3%) to 66/75 (88.0%). Sustainability beyond the initial period was not assessed.
